description: ASET-RSET maps is the reference implementation of a method that maps, over a building floor plan, the margin between the available safe egress time (ASET, when conditions become untenable in a fire) and the required safe egress time (RSET, when occupants have left), instead of comparing the two at a few points. It was written by Benjamin Schröder (Görtzen Stolbrink & Partner) with Lukas Arnold and Armin Seyfried (Forschungszentrum Jülich and University of Wuppertal) for their 2020 Fire Safety Journal paper and includes a base-case demonstration scenario. Coverage is any building or enclosed public space modelled with the Fire Dynamics Simulator. Access: release v1.0.1 archived on Zenodo on 3 June 2020, with the source in the FireDynamics GitHub organisation. Licence: open (Zenodo 'other-open'; terms in the repository); free. Caveats: a research reference implementation that needs FDS results and evacuation inputs; not updated since 2020. Simulation uses: performance-based fire safety design and evacuation assessment of buildings, stations and venues. Related records: JuPedSim and Vadere for the pedestrian side, Fire Dynamics Simulator for smoke and heat.
